Dresses for Christmas Party Season That Will Make You Actually Excited to Get Dressed

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 15:56
Instaread

Dresses for Christmas party season should feel fun to shop for. And yet somehow every year it turns into a longer process than it needs to be: too many options, too many occasions with different dress codes, too much uncertainty about what actually looks good versus what just looks festive in the product photo. I have done enough holiday dress searching to know what actually works and what photographs well but feels uncomfortable by 8 PM and ends up shoved in the back of the closet by January. This post covers the styles that deliver on both counts (beautiful and actually wearable), organized by silhouette, occasion and what to pair each one with so you can shop with a clear picture of what you are looking for.

The quick answer: The best dresses for Christmas party season are a velvet midi (the most versatile), a sequin dress (the most festive), a classic red dress, a satin slip dress, a wrap dress and a plaid or tartan dress. For the office party I go with velvet or a jewel tone wrap dress, for a casual get-together plaid is perfect and for a formal dinner I reach for sequins, satin or a maxi.

The Velvet Dress: The Holiday Season Non-Negotiable

If there is one fabric that owns December it is velvet. A velvet dress photographs beautifully, holds its shape through a full evening, has the specific luxurious quality that reads as festive without being costumey and is warmer than it looks, which matters when you are walking from a parking garage to a restaurant in the cold.

The velvet midi dress is the most versatile silhouette in this category. Long enough to feel elegant and appropriate for almost any holiday occasion, short enough to show off great boots or heels and structured enough to work on its own without a lot of additional styling effort. A forest green, deep burgundy or rich navy velvet midi is the dress you can wear to the office holiday party, your neighborhood dinner party, a more formal family gathering and your best friend’s Christmas cocktail party in the same season with different accessories and look appropriate and beautiful for all of them.

How to wear it: A velvet midi dress with block-heeled ankle boots or strappy heeled sandals and a simple clutch. Gold jewelry (earrings and a delicate necklace) keeps it warm and festive without overdoing it. A slim-fit blazer over the top for an office party transitions the look toward more professional without losing the holiday feel.

For the formal end of the occasion spectrum our rehearsal dinner dress post at frostedevents.com/rehearsal-dinner-dress/ covers the elevated occasion dressing approach that applies directly to the more formal Christmas dinner or party, the velvet midi sits perfectly in this category.

The Sequin Dress: When You Want to Fully Commit

A sequin dress for the Christmas party is a full commitment and I mean that in the best possible way. It is the option that requires zero additional styling effort because the dress does all the work. It is also the option that produces the best photos, gets the most compliments and makes you feel exactly as festive as the season deserves.

The sequin mini dress is the most classic format, above the knee, figure-forward and unambiguous about the fact that this is a party. The sequin midi is the more elevated alternative, longer, slightly more formal and easier to wear on nights when you want the sparkle without the shorter hemline. Both are right depending on the occasion and your personal comfort level.

Gold sequin is the most universally flattering and the most broadly Christmas-appropriate color in the sequin category. It coordinates with warm jewelry and warm accessories and photographs beautifully against almost any background. Silver sequin is cooler-toned and more modern, beautiful on cooler skin tones and very effective against a white or winter backdrop. Black sequin is the most sophisticated option and the one that transitions most easily between a holiday party and a New Year’s Eve event in the same season.

How to wear it: A sequin dress is the star. Keep everything else simple. Nude or metallic strappy heels. A small clutch in a complementary metallic. Simple stud earrings. A chandelier earring competes with the dress rather than complementing it. A solid-colored coat in a neutral or rich color so the sequin peek beneath the hem as you walk in does the dramatic reveal work.

The Red Dress: The Classic That Never Disappoints

The red dress for a Christmas party is a classic for the specific reason that it works, every single time, for virtually every woman, in virtually every holiday setting. It is not the most original choice and it is exactly right regardless.

The silhouette matters more than anything else in the red dress category because a well-fitted red dress is stunning and a poorly-fitted red dress is just a red dress. Look for styles with built-in structure: a wrap style that creates a natural waist, a fit-and-flare silhouette that moves beautifully or a tailored sheath that is clean and polished.

Fabric elevates everything in red. A red velvet dress hits differently than a red polyester dress at the same price point and the difference is immediately visible in photos. Red satin is glamorous and formal. Red crepe is elegant and drapes well. Whatever the silhouette, investing in a quality fabric pays off in how the dress photographs and how it feels to wear it through a full evening.

How to wear it: A red Christmas party dress needs almost no additional color. Black heels or nude heels, a black or gold clutch, gold jewelry in simple shapes. The red is the color story. Let it be.

The Satin Slip Dress: The Elevated Minimalist Option

For the woman who finds heavily embellished or brightly colored holiday dresses overwhelming the satin slip dress is the Christmas party option that feels sophisticated, intentional and genuinely beautiful without asking you to be anyone you are not.

A champagne, blush, ivory or deep bronze satin slip dress is the holiday party option that looks expensive in the specific understated way that requires nothing extra to pull off. The satin catches light, moves beautifully and photographs with a luminous quality that sequins approach from a different direction.

The slip dress format (a simple, bias-cut or straight-cut satin in a midi or maxi length) is the style that works best for this aesthetic. The length and the fabric together create the elevated feeling. Pair it with sculptural heels or pointed-toe flats and minimalist jewelry and the look is complete.

Layering the slip dress for warmth and additional interest: a fitted ribbed turtleneck underneath in a contrasting or complementary color, a slim-fit blazer over the top or a longline cardigan make the slip dress appropriate for the full range of December temperatures without compromising the look.

The Wrap Dress: The One That Works on Every Body

The wrap dress is the most universally flattering silhouette in existence and during the Christmas party season it is one of the most practical and most consistently beautiful options available.

The wrap format creates a natural waist on every body, allows for easy sizing adjustments (the tie makes the fit infinitely adjustable) and moves in a way that is both comfortable and elegant throughout a full evening of standing, sitting and everything in between. It also photographs beautifully from every angle because the diagonal neckline and tied waist create a naturally dynamic silhouette.

For the holidays specifically: a wrap dress in a rich jewel tone (emerald, sapphire, deep plum, cranberry) in a matte crepe or a more festive metallic fabric. The wrap silhouette in a festive color is the formula that works for literally every holiday party occasion from the most casual neighborhood gathering to the most formal work dinner.

How to wear it: Heeled boots make a wrap midi feel complete and keep the legs warm. A block heel or low kitten heel keeps it comfortable for a full evening. A delicate gold chain necklace and simple earrings are all the jewelry this silhouette needs.

The Plaid or Tartan Dress: The Underrated Holiday Option

Plaid gets underestimated as a Christmas party dress option and should not. A well-cut plaid or tartan dress in classic Christmas colorways (red and green, red and black, navy and green) is festive without being over the top and photographs beautifully in the specific warm, traditional way that velvet and sequin do not.

The plaid shirt dress or plaid A-line mini in a quality fabric with clean tailoring is the dress that looks effortlessly seasonal without reading as a costume. It is the option for the woman who wants to feel Christmas-y without doing a full sequin or velvet moment, and it is genuinely more interesting and less predictable than either.

How to wear it: Over-the-knee boots or ankle boots in dark brown or black. A cream or camel turtleneck underneath for colder evenings. Tortoiseshell or gold accessories rather than silver. The warm tones in plaid coordinate with warm metals.

Which Christmas Party Dress to Wear for Each Type of Party

The Office Holiday Party

The office party requires the most careful calibration of any holiday occasion, festive enough to participate in the season, appropriate enough for a professional setting. The velvet midi, the wrap dress in a jewel tone and the satin slip dress in a more covered silhouette are all excellent choices. Avoid anything too short, too revealing or too heavily sequined unless your workplace specifically has a reputation for going all-in on the holiday party dress code.

Helping plan the party too? My get-together ideas for adult friend groups and 25 Christmas party appetizers make hosting easy. If you are a guest, grab one of these hostess gifts on your way out the door, and if you want a theme, my Grinchmas party ideas are so much fun.

The Neighborhood or Casual Gathering

This is where you have the most freedom. The red wrap dress, the plaid dress with over-the-knee boots, the velvet midi with ankle boots. All of these land at exactly the right festive-but-approachable level for a casual holiday gathering. This is also the occasion where you can go a little more fashion-forward or experimental than you might at a more formal event.

The Formal Christmas Dinner or Party

The sequin midi, the satin maxi or the velvet gown-length option are all appropriate for the most formal end of the Christmas party spectrum. At this level of formality the length tends to be longer (midi or maxi), the fabric is more luxurious and the overall silhouette is more formal. Heels, a small formal clutch and more elaborate jewelry are all appropriate. For a true black tie event, my black tie wedding guest dress guide has floor-length options that work just as well for a formal holiday gala.

What to Wear With a Christmas Party Dress

Shoes: A strappy heeled sandal is the most versatile shoe for most Christmas party dresses and works across almost every silhouette. For midi and maxi lengths heeled ankle boots or pointed-toe boots in a complementary color are equally appropriate and significantly warmer. A block heel is more comfortable for long evenings than a stiletto. Prioritize comfort for any party that involves significant standing or dancing.

Jewelry: For heavily embellished dresses (sequin, velvet with embroidery, beaded), keep jewelry simple and small. For more minimalist dresses (satin slip, wrap, plaid), a more statement earring or necklace adds the interest the dress does not provide on its own. Gold jewelry photographs warmer and tends to be more universally flattering in holiday settings than silver. My capsule jewelry collection covers the pieces I reach for most and these affordable luxury jewelry picks look far more expensive than they are.

Bag: A small clutch in a metallic, a rich jewel tone or a simple black keeps the accessory focused. A crossbody in a festive fabric is more practical for events where you need your hands free. Many holiday party clutches end up being handed to someone else or left on a chair.

Outerwear: A tailored wool coat or a faux fur wrap in a neutral color allows the dress to be the statement while keeping you genuinely warm in the cold. A full-length coat that reaches the hem of the dress looks the most polished. A few of the fall jackets everyone is buying right now look just as good over a party dress.

Finding Your Size on Amazon

Amazon has become one of the best sources for Christmas party dresses at every price point and the size range (including extended sizes) is genuinely excellent. A few tips for buying dresses on Amazon:

Read the size chart measurements rather than relying on S/M/L designations. Sizing varies significantly by brand and the measurements are the only reliable guide. Read reviews specifically from people with your body type or measurements for the most useful fit information. Order two sizes if you are between sizes. Amazon’s return process is straightforward and having both options to try at home is more practical than trying to guess from a product photo.

Christmas Party Dress FAQ

What is the best dress style for a Christmas party?

The velvet midi dress is the most universally flattering and most broadly appropriate style for the widest range of Christmas party occasions. It photographs beautifully, keeps you warmer than a shorter or lighter-weight dress and works across everything from a casual neighborhood gathering to a formal company dinner with different accessories. The wrap dress is the most flattering for every body type. The sequin dress is the most festive and most photograph-forward choice.

What color dress is best for a Christmas party?

Deep jewel tones (forest green, burgundy, sapphire and deep plum) are the most broadly flattering and most consistently festive choices for a Christmas party dress. Red is the classic Christmas party color and always works. Gold and champagne are the most glamorous options. Black is the most sophisticated and the most flexible across different occasion levels.

Can you wear a short dress to a Christmas party?

Yes, depending on the occasion. A sequin mini or a velvet mini dress is entirely appropriate for a casual holiday party, a cocktail party or any gathering with a festive dress code. For a more formal dinner or an office party a midi or maxi length tends to read as more polished and appropriate.

What shoes go best with a Christmas party dress?

Strappy heeled sandals work with almost every Christmas party dress silhouette and are the most versatile option. Block-heeled ankle boots or pointed-toe boots are excellent with midi and maxi lengths and keep legs warmer in cold weather. For maximum comfort through a long evening choose a block heel or a low kitten heel over a stiletto.

What do you wear over a Christmas party dress in winter?

A tailored wool coat in a neutral color (camel, black, charcoal or deep navy) is the most polished outerwear option over a Christmas party dress. A faux fur wrap or stole adds glamour for more formal occasions. A long cardigan in a complementary color works for more casual gatherings. Avoid a puffer coat over a formal dress if at all possible: check it at the door rather than wearing it into the party.

What should I wear to an office Christmas party?

Pick something festive but polished: a velvet midi, a wrap dress in a jewel tone or a satin slip dress layered with a blazer or cardigan. Keep the hemline at or just above the knee and save the full sequin mini for after-hours parties.

Is Amazon a good place to buy a Christmas party dress?

Yes. Amazon has party dresses at every price point and a great extended size range. Shop by the size chart measurements instead of S/M/L, read reviews from women with your build and order two sizes if you are in between since returns are easy.
